Consult Summary:
- Acute unilateral left-sided migraine-like headache with visual disturbances and nausea/vomiting starting this morning; plan includes self-care and NSAID/antiemetic approach with same-day neurological assessment if needed.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Very strong, sudden-onset headache this morning with dizziness, blurred vision described as zigzag lines, and nausea/vomiting (vomited twice). Pain is left-sided and worsened by movement; patient desires head to remain still. Concerned about serious causes (brain tumor or stroke).
- Timeline: Headache started this morning with sudden onset; paracetamol taken ~3 hours ago with little to no relief; current pain estimated around 6/10 (compared to kidney stone as 10/10); visual symptoms persist.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Movement worsens symptoms; rest/lying still preferred; paracetamol did not relieve.
- Associated symptoms: Dizziness; blurred vision with zigzag lines; nausea; two episodes of vomiting; dislikes screens due to visual disturbance.
- Neurological symptoms: No weakness reported; no gait disturbance; walking appears normal.
- Prior similar headaches: Not experienced before; first-time presentation of this pattern; mother has migraines (family history).
- Medications: Paracetamol taken; no regular medications.
- Pregnancy: Question asked; patient doubts pregnancy; no evidence of pregnancy.
- Allergies: None known per patient.
- Past Medical History: Kidney stones noted in history.
- Social History: Not documented.
- Family History: Migraine in mother; hypothyroidism in mother. Partial/conflicting information about thyroid disease (hyperthyroidism mentioned by clinician, patient states mother has hypothyroidism); conflict noted.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute migraine with associated visual disturbances and nausea/vomiting
  - Plan:
    - OTC ibuprofen (ibuprofen) with anti-sickness (antiemetic) as needed
    - Recommend ingestion of sugary, carbonated drinks (e.g., Coca-Cola) as supportive measure
    - If available, consider migraine-specific relief medication if OTC options fail
    - Monitor response: improvement expected within 30–40 minutes; if symptoms persist or worsen, proceed with further evaluation
    - In the interim, patient advised to avoid or minimize screen exposure
    - Urgent/same-day neurological assessment planned if symptoms persist or if there are any new neurological signs
    - If symptoms improve before the appointment, patient may cancel the appointment
- Issue 2: Need for neurological assessment
  - Plan:
    - Assess with a full neurological examination at the scheduled time today or sooner if symptoms worsen
- Issue 3: Safety-netting and follow-up
  - Plan:
    - If symptoms worsen, or new neurological deficits develop (e.g., weakness, speech disturbance), seek urgent care
    - Contact clinic if there are any changes or questions prior to the planned assessment

General Plan:
- Proceed with symptomatic migraine management and arrange same-day neurological assessment to confirm diagnosis and rule out red flags.
- If improvements occur with OTC therapy, consider canceling planned appointment.
